etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French caresse, from Italian carezza (“dear”), from Latin cārus (“dear”), from Proto-Indo-European *keh₂-, akin to Sanskrit काम (kāma, “love”). Doublet of karezza.

definitions.definition: An act of endearment; any act or expression of affection; an embracing, or touching, with tenderness. [from 1640s]

quote.citation: 1849–1861, Thomas Babington Macaulay, chapter XVII, in The History of England from the Accession of James the Second, volume (please specify |volume=I to V), London: Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, →OCLC:
quote.text: He exerted himself to win by indulgence and caresses the hearts of all who were under his command.

quote.citation: 1855 November 10, Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, “The Four Winds”, in The Song of Hiawatha, Boston, Mass.: Ticknor and Fields, →OCLC, page 26:
quote.text: And he wooed her with his soft caresses, / Wooed her with his smile of sunshine,  […]

definitions.definition: (transitive) To touch or kiss lovingly; to fondle.
(transitive) To affect as if with a caress.

quote.text: The love and anguish in his voice caressed my mind and soul.
